patterns.comment: global preset variables, not lexer keywords -- pi/euler/phi/psi are BigFloat constants set at startup
patterns.name: constant.language.cnr

patterns.comment: real control-flow/statement keywords recognized by the lexer's keywordTable(); this language has no break/continue/switch/case/default/do/import/using/namespace
patterns.name: keyword.control.cnr

patterns.comment: only these have dedicated TokType entries; there is no bool/void/double keyword -- double-precision numbers are just the language's native 'var' number type
patterns.name: storage.type.cnr

patterns.comment: (Type)expr casts -- the only ones the parser recognizes: (char), (char[]), (string), (Int), (long), (Float), (BigInt), (BigFloat) or (BigFloat(precision)). There is no (bool) or (double) cast. The inner (precision) in BigFloat(N) is left to #numbers/#operators to scope as an ordinary parenthesized number.
patterns.name: storage.type.cast.cnr

patterns.comment: var[] is an array, var[][] a Matrix, var[][][]+ a Tensor -- all the same 'var' keyword with repeated brackets, not separate Matrix()/Tensor() constructors (those don't exist as callables)
patterns.name: storage.type.matrix.cnr

patterns.comment: Struct Name { ... } -- Name is the type being declared
complete builtin math-function whitelist from isMathBuiltinName() -- note arcsin/arccos/arctan (not asin/acos/atan), and ln alongside log/log10
patterns.name: support.function.cnr

patterns.comment: MathLib bridge builtins (math_bridge.inc) -- symbolic function definition/calculus/domain/limits, all keyed by a mathDefine()'d function name string
patterns.name: support.function.mathlib.cnr

patterns.comment: MathLib bridge builtins for Matrix values (var[][] arrays)
patterns.name: support.function.matlib.cnr

patterns.comment: request/response are ordinary scope-bound objects inside route handlers, not lexer keywords -- highlighted as known globals, not as language keywords
patterns.name: variable.language.cnr

patterns.comment: Nodes NAME { StepA() { ... }; StepB(StepA) -> OnFail(Retry = N) { ... }; }
patterns.name: keyword.control.nodes.cnr

patterns.comment: the complete operator/punctuation set the lexer actually tokenizes (Plus..GreaterEqual, AndAnd/OrOr/Bang, Dot/Colon) -- this language has no ++/--/+=/-=/*=//=/%=/<</>>/::/? tokens. '->' is kept only because Nodes blocks write `Step() -> OnFail(...)`, tokenized as separate '-' and '>' but read as an arrow.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.cnr
